title: Dill and Cucumber Tzatziki
summary: Thick Greek yoghurt with salted, squeezed cucumber, plenty of dill, lemon and a thread of olive oil, chilled until the garlic softens.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
garlic cloves, grated to a paste
dill, finely chopped, plus a sprig to serve
extra-virgin olive oil, plus a drizzle to serve
fine sea salt or table salt

steps.title: Grate and salt
steps.text: Coarsely grate the unpeeled cucumber, toss it with 0.25 tsp salt in the sieve and let it sit for 10 min. Salt draws water out of the cucumber cells, so the dip stays thick instead of turning runny in the fridge.

steps.title: Wring it dry
steps.text: Pile the cucumber into the clean tea towel, twist the ends and squeeze hard over the sink. You should end up with a compact, barely damp handful.

steps.title: Build the sauce
steps.text: In the mixing bowl, stir together the yoghurt, garlic paste, chopped dill, lemon juice, 2 tbsp olive oil, the remaining salt and the pepper. Fold the cucumber through last so it keeps a little crunch.

steps.title: Let it chill
steps.text: Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 min. Resting lets the sharp garlic spread out and soften, and the yoghurt firms up again once cold.

steps.title: Swirl and serve
steps.text: Spoon the tzatziki into a serving bowl and drag the back of the spoon round to make a shallow swirl. Pool a little olive oil in the hollow and finish with a sprig of dill.

tips: Skipping the squeeze is the most common mistake; unsqueezed cucumber leaks water and thins the dip within an hour.
Use strained Greek-style yoghurt; ordinary plain yoghurt is too loose for a scoopable dip.
Grate the garlic finely so it disperses evenly rather than leaving hot little pieces.
Swap half the dill for chopped mint for a fresher, cooler note.
storage: Keep covered in the fridge for up to 3 days; stir before serving, as a little liquid may collect on top. Do not freeze, as the yoghurt separates. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
